messages:
maria: Heads-up — overnight we saw a burst of ECC parity faults + a small cluster of Xid 13s on a handful of gpu nodes in us-west-2 (nodes: gpu-w2-102, gpu-w2-321). Telemetry shows ~70 ECC events in 10m for gpu-w2-321 and 3 Xid 13 in the same window. Can we discuss an automated cordon/drain policy?

alex: Ugh, saw the alerts. Are these nodes still passing application health checks?

maria: app-level probes are flaky (some pods OOMing), but control plane is fine. Noticed kernel logs with repeated `GPU: Xid 13` and `EccError: corrected` lines.

neha: My 2¢ — we should avoid instantaneous drains for single corrected ECCs. Need a score-based debounce: accumulate ECC count + Xid occurrences over a sliding window, then cordon when threshold crossed.

samir: Agree. Proposed scoring: +1 per corrected ECC, +10 per Xid 13, +30 for Xid 31/43. Trigger cordon at score >= 50 in 10m, immediate drain if score >= 100 or if we see a job kill from NV.

maria: Love the scoring idea. Also need different behavior for K8s vs Slurm: K8s -> cordon + graceful drain; Slurm -> set NODE state=DRAIN and requeue small jobs.

neha: Draft k8s action (example):
```
# cordon + graceful drain
kubectl cordon NODE_NAME
kubectl drain NODE_NAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m
```
For Slurm: `scontrol update NodeName=NODE_NAME State=DRAIN Reason="gpu-healthwatch:score>=50"` then `scontrol requeue` for running jobs depending on priority/policy.

alex: Who will own the actuator? We don't want the alert -> flaky webhook that blips nodes repeatedly. Need leader election + backoff + rate limits.

infra-bot: [alertmanager] GPU ECC spike detected for cluster us-west-2: gpu-w2-321 (score=72). Alert fired at 2026-07-17T02:14:12Z.

samir: infra-bot good timing. Operator responsibilities: 1) healthwatch collector emits prometheus metric gpu_health_score{node="..."}, 2) alertmanager rule with for: 1m -> webhook to autocordon-controller, 3) controller calculates final decision using smoothing window + suppressed if node was already acted on in last 30m.

maria: We should also mark node with label `gpu.health=quarantine` and a taint `gpu/quarantine:NoExecute` instead of immediate drain in borderline cases — prevents new pods from landing while keeping current workloads for a short grace period.

neha: Yep. Flow idea: score 50-99 -> cordon + taint (quarantine) + notify SRE + attempt graceful drain with 30m timeout. score >=100 or Xid severity high -> cordon + immediate drain + trigger replacement workflow (terminate and reprovision).

samir: Replacement policy: if node is quarantined twice within 24h OR has >200 ECC/day -> auto-put into replacement pool and spin up spare GPU. Need cost guardrails: prefer spare from reserved pool before launching new spot instance.

alex: Can we simulate on staging? We should add a canary: apply autocordon-controller to a single node pool, create synthetic ECC/Xid signals, verify no false-positive drains for short blips.

maria: I'll own the staging test. Will also add metrics dashboard: ECC rate, Xid count, node score timeline, drains triggered, replacement counts. Link to runbook (draft): https://go.redwood/runbooks/gpu-health-autocordon :eyes:

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook created (draft) at https://go.redwood/runbooks/gpu-health-autocordon. Steps: detect -> score -> cordon/taint -> drain policy -> replacement. Includes rollback instructions and manual override commands.

alex: One more practical item: include a cooldown after a drain where the controller marks the node `gpu.health=investigated` for 1h to prevent repeated actions while humans check.

maria: Agreed. Also add a fallback: if drain fails due to unschedulable pods, escalate to human and don't auto-terminate.

neha: I'll put together the alerting rule and a PoC controller repo with leader election and a simulation harness. Plan: PoC -> staging runbook -> 2-week canary -> prod rollout.

samir: Sounds good. Action items: neha (PoC + alert rules), maria (staging test + dashboards + runbook updates), alex (cost/replacement policy), samir (Slurm integration hooks). I'll draft the PR for the scoring thresholds and controller API by EOD. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — let's try to keep the thresholds conservative initially. If anyone notices additional noisy signals from other regions, mention them here.

infra-bot: Noted. Will synthesize alerts into the testing channel during the canary. :robot_face:
